title: The Person Who Tied the Bell Must Untie It
synopsis: The Chinese proverb "the person who tied the bell must untie it" is used to convey the idea that the person who created a problem is the one who should resolve it. The proverb originates from a story about a rebellious but wise monk who lived during the Northern Song Dynasty

fullText.simplified:
解铃还须系铃人

    生活中人人都会遇到问题，大部分问题都不难解决。但如果遇到非常麻烦的问题，就需要智慧了，“解铃还须系铃人”说的就是这种情况。
    中国北宋年间，有一个叫法灯的小和尚，在南京的一所寺院里出家。佛教的规矩非常多，对和尚们的要求很高，比如：不能杀害动物、不能偷东西、不能说谎、不能喝酒等等。对于这些规矩，法灯不以为然。他经常喝酒，喝醉以后就整天睡觉，什么都不干，这让他在寺院里不太受欢迎。但寺院的住持很欣赏他，认为他是一个很有智慧的人。住持认为佛教设立规矩的目的是希望大家可以内心平静，追求智慧，而法灯已经内心平静、很有智慧了，所以他对法灯不守规矩的行为并不生气。
    一次，住持带着和尚们一起讨论问题，他问道：“一个金铃铛系在老虎的脖子上，你们谁能把它解下来？”和尚们你看我，我看你，都无法回答。和尚不能回答杀死老虎，因为佛教规定不能随便杀动物；他们也不能回答自己去拿，因为老虎会吃人。这时，法灯慢慢地说：“谁系上去的，就去找谁解下来就可以了。”和尚们觉得法灯的回答精彩极了，他们终于理解了住持的观点：法灯是一个很有智慧的人。
    这就是“解铃还须系铃人”的故事。这个故事用解开老虎脖子上的金铃铛来比喻困难或者麻烦，想要解决问题，先要找到问题的根源，就是把铃铛系上去的人，因为如果这个人有能力把铃铛系到老虎的脖子上，他自然就有能力把铃铛解下来。生活中的麻烦同样如此，只要找到麻烦的根源，就很容易解决麻烦了。所以这个俗语用来表达一种解决问题的思路：处理问题的关键在于认识、找到问题的源头，只有如此才能快速和彻底地解决问题。
    现在，如果你听到有人说：“这都是老汪惹出来的麻烦，解铃还须系铃人，我明天就去找他谈谈。”你能明白他的意思吗？
fullText.traditional:
解鈴還須繫鈴人

    生活中人人都會遇到問題，大部分問題都不難解決。但如果遇到非常麻煩的問題，就需要智慧了，“解鈴還須繫鈴人”說的就是這種情況。
    中國北宋年間，有一個叫法燈的小和尚，在南京的一所寺院裡出家。佛教的規矩非常多，對和尚們的要求很高，比如：不能殺害動物、不能偷東西、不能說謊、不能喝酒等等。對於這些規矩，法燈不以為然。他經常喝酒，喝醉以後就整天睡覺，什麼都不幹，這讓他在寺院裡不太受歡迎。但寺院的住持很欣賞他，認為他是一個很有智慧的人。住持認為佛教設立規矩的目的是希望大家可以內心平靜，追求智慧，而法燈已經內心平靜、很有智慧了，所以他對法燈不守規矩的行為並不生氣。
    一次，住持帶著和尚們一起討論問題，他問道：“一個金鈴鐺繫在老虎的脖子上，你們誰能把它解下來？”和尚們你看我，我看你，都無法回答。和尚不能回答殺死老虎，因為佛教規定不能隨便殺動物；他們也不能回答自己去拿，因為老虎會吃人。這時，法燈慢慢地說：“誰繫上去的，就去找誰解下來就可以了。”和尚們覺得法燈的回答精彩極了，他們終於理解了住持的觀點：法燈是一個很有智慧的人。
    這就是“解鈴還須繫鈴人”的故事。這個故事用解開老虎脖子上的金鈴鐺來比喻困難或者麻煩，想要解決問題，先要找到問題的根源，就是把鈴鐺繫上去的人，因為如果這個人有能力把鈴鐺繫到老虎的脖子上，他自然就有能力把鈴鐺解下來。生活中的麻煩同樣如此，只要找到麻煩的根源，就很容易解決麻煩了。所以這個俗語用來表達一種解決問題的思路：處理問題的關鍵在於認識、找到問題的源頭，只有如此才能快速和徹底地解決問題。
    現在，如果你聽到有人說：“這都是老汪惹出來的麻煩，解鈴還須繫鈴人，我明天就去找他談談。”你能明白他的意思嗎？

sentences.english: He often drank, and when he was drunk, he would sleep all day and do nothing, which made him unpopular in the temple.

sentences.traditional: 住持認為佛教設立規矩的目的是希望大家可以內心平靜，追求智慧，
sentences.pinyin: zhù chí rèn wéi fó jiào shè lì guī ju de mù dì shì xī wàng dà jiā kě yǐ nèi xīn píng jìng zhuī qiú zhì huì
sentences.english: But the abbot of the temple admired him very much and thought he was a very wise man.

sentences.simplified: 而法灯已经内心平静、很有智慧了，所以他对法灯不守规矩的行为并不生气。
sentences.traditional: 而法燈已經內心平靜、很有智慧了，所以他對法燈不守規矩的行為並不生氣。
sentences.pinyin: ér fǎ dēng yǐ jīng nèi xīn píng jìng hěn yǒu zhì huì le suǒ yǐ tā duì fǎ dēng bù shǒu guī ju de xíng wéi bìng bù shēng qì
sentences.english: The abbot believed that the purpose of the rules established by Buddhism was to help everyone find inner peace and pursue wisdom.
And since Fadeng was already at peace and very wise, the abbot was not upset by Fadeng’s disregard for the rules.

sentences.traditional: 他問道：“一個金鈴鐺繫在老虎的脖子上，你們誰能把它解下來？”
sentences.pinyin: tā wèn dào yí ge jīn líng dang xì zài lǎo hǔ de bó zi shang nǐ men shéi néng bǎ tā jiě xià lai
sentences.english: Once, the abbot gathered the monks to discuss a problem.

sentences.traditional: 和尚們你看我，我看你，都無法回答。
sentences.pinyin: hé shang men nǐ kàn wǒ wǒ kàn nǐ dōu wú fǎ huí dá
sentences.english: He asked, “A golden bell is tied around the neck of a tiger. Who among you can take it off?”

sentences.simplified: 和尚不能回答杀死老虎，因为佛教规定不能随便杀动物；
sentences.traditional: 和尚不能回答殺死老虎，因為佛教規定不能隨便殺動物；
sentences.pinyin: hé shang bù néng huí dá shā sǐ lǎo hǔ yīn wèi fó jiào guī dìng bù néng suí biàn shā dòng wù
sentences.english: The monks looked at each other, but none of them could answer.

sentences.simplified: 他们也不能回答自己去拿，因为老虎会吃人。
sentences.traditional: 他們也不能回答自己去拿，因為老虎會吃人。

sentences.english: The monks could not answer that they should kill the tiger because Buddhism stipulates that animals cannot be killed arbitrarily.

sentences.simplified: 这时，法灯慢慢地说：“谁系上去的，就去找谁解下来就可以了。”
sentences.traditional: 這時，法燈慢慢地說：“誰繫上去的，就去找誰解下來就可以了。”
sentences.pinyin: zhè shí fǎ dēng màn man de shuō shéi xì shàng qù de jiù qù zhǎo shéi jiě xià lái jiù kě yǐ le
sentences.english: They also could not answer that they would do it themselves because the tiger would eat people.

sentences.simplified: 和尚们觉得法灯的回答精彩极了，他们终于理解了住持的观点：法灯是一个很有智慧的人。
sentences.traditional: 和尚們覺得法燈的回答精彩極了，他們終於理解了住持的觀點：法燈是一個很有智慧的人。
sentences.pinyin: hé shang men jué de fǎ dēng de huí dá jīng cǎi jí le tā men zhōng yú lǐ jiě le zhù chí de guān diǎn fǎ dēng shì yí ge hěn yǒu zhì huì de rén
sentences.english: At this time, Fadeng slowly said, “Just find the person who tied it in the first place and have them untie it.”
The monks thought Fadeng’s answer was brilliant, and they finally understood the abbot’s point of view: Fadeng was a very wise man.

sentences.traditional: 這就是“解鈴還須繫鈴人”的故事。

sentences.simplified: 这个故事用解开老虎脖子上的金铃铛来比喻困难或者麻烦，
sentences.traditional: 這個故事用解開老虎脖子上的金鈴鐺來比喻困難或者麻煩，
sentences.pinyin: zhè ge gù shi yòng jiě kāi lǎo hǔ bó zi shang de jīn líng dang lái bǐ yù kùn nan huò zhě má fan
sentences.english: This is the story of “the person who tied the bell must untie it”.

sentences.simplified: 想要解决问题，先要找到问题的根源，就是把铃铛系上去的人，
sentences.traditional: 想要解決問題，先要找到問題的根源，就是把鈴鐺繫上去的人，

sentences.english: This story uses the untying of the golden bell from the tiger’s neck as a metaphor for difficulties or troubles.

sentences.simplified: 因为如果这个人有能力把铃铛系到老虎的脖子上，他自然就有能力把铃铛解下来。
sentences.traditional: 因為如果這個人有能力把鈴鐺繫到老虎的脖子上，他自然就有能力把鈴鐺解下來。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi rú guǒ zhè ge rén yǒu néng lì bǎ líng dang xì dào lǎo hǔ de bó zi shang tā zì rán jiù yǒu néng lì bǎ líng dang jiě xià lái
sentences.english: If you want to solve a problem, you must first find the root of the problem, which is the person who tied the bell.

sentences.simplified: 生活中的麻烦同样如此，只要找到麻烦的根源，就很容易解决麻烦了。
sentences.traditional: 生活中的麻煩同樣如此，只要找到麻煩的根源，就很容易解決麻煩了。
sentences.pinyin: shēng huó zhōng de má fan tóng yàng rú cǐ zhǐ yào zhǎo dào má fan de gēn yuán jiù hěn róng yì jiě jué má fan le
sentences.english: Because if this person had the ability to tie the bell around the tiger’s neck, he naturally has the ability to untie the bell.

sentences.english: The same is true for troubles in life. As long as you find the root cause of the trouble, it will be easy to solve.

sentences.simplified: 处理问题的关键在于认识、找到问题的源头，
sentences.traditional: 處理問題的關鍵在於認識、找到問題的源頭，

sentences.english: Therefore, this proverb is used to express a way of thinking about solving problems:

sentences.simplified: 只有如此才能快速和彻底地解决问题。
sentences.traditional: 只有如此才能快速和徹底地解決問題。
sentences.pinyin: zhǐ yǒu rú cǐ cái néng kuài sù hé chè dǐ de jiě jué wèn tí
sentences.english: The key to solving problems is to understand and find the source of the problem.
Only in this way can the problem be solved quickly and thoroughly.

sentences.english: Now, if you hear someone say, ..

sentence_translations: The Person Who Tied the Bell Must Untie It
Everyone encounters problems in life, and most problems are not difficult to solve.
But if you encounter a very troublesome problem, you need wisdom.
“The person who tied the bell must be the one to untie it” refers to this kind of situation.
During the Northern Song Dynasty in China, there was a young monk named Fadeng who entered a temple in Nanjing.
Buddhism has many rules and high demands for monks, such as: not killing animals, not stealing, not lying, not drinking alcohol, and so on.
Fadeng objected to these rules.
He often drank, and when he was drunk, he would sleep all day and do nothing, which made him unpopular in the temple.
But the abbot of the temple admired him very much and thought he was a very wise man.
The abbot believed that the purpose of the rules established by Buddhism was to help everyone find inner peace and pursue wisdom.
And since Fadeng was already at peace and very wise, the abbot was not upset by Fadeng’s disregard for the rules.
Once, the abbot gathered the monks to discuss a problem.
He asked, “A golden bell is tied around the neck of a tiger. Who among you can take it off?”
The monks looked at each other, but none of them could answer.
The monks could not answer that they should kill the tiger because Buddhism stipulates that animals cannot be killed arbitrarily.
They also could not answer that they would do it themselves because the tiger would eat people.
At this time, Fadeng slowly said, “Just find the person who tied it in the first place and have them untie it.”
The monks thought Fadeng’s answer was brilliant, and they finally understood the abbot’s point of view: Fadeng was a very wise man.
This is the story of “the person who tied the bell must untie it”.
This story uses the untying of the golden bell from the tiger’s neck as a metaphor for difficulties or troubles.
If you want to solve a problem, you must first find the root of the problem, which is the person who tied the bell.
Because if this person had the ability to tie the bell around the tiger’s neck, he naturally has the ability to untie the bell.
The same is true for troubles in life. As long as you find the root cause of the trouble, it will be easy to solve.
Therefore, this proverb is used to express a way of thinking about solving problems:
The key to solving problems is to understand and find the source of the problem.
Only in this way can the problem be solved quickly and thoroughly.
Now, if you hear someone say, ..
“This trouble was caused by Old Wang. The person who tied the bell must untie it. I’ll go talk to him tomorrow,” ..
.. can you understand what they mean?”
